text:
Darnell Nurse spent nearly 800 games in Edmonton before landing in San Jose, where he's an alternate captain playing over 21 minutes a night. The early returns have been quiet: two points in 18 games, and his name has already shown up in mock-trade pieces (Markerzone had him headed to Detroit in one). That's the kind of attention that comes with his contract and his role.

The Sharks have taken 42% of the expected goals with him on the ice, close to the team's level, so he isn't dragging them down as much as the point total suggests. His shooting is cold, 3.4%, and last season Evolving-Hockey noted he was better than his goals, with the chances there and the finishing or goaltending behind him not.

What he still brings is skating, faster than 89% of the league by NHL Edge, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him exiting the zone with possession more than half the time. Our range says 13 to 28 points over a full season. On a young team, he's there to absorb hard minutes and steady the room. The scoring is a bonus.
headline: Nurse settles into a new room
